transcript.text: (gentle rock music)
- These guys have saved our lives.
We've been in water all day, since, actually last night,
and we didn't think help was coming until you guys came,
and I thank you so much 'cause I've got not just myself
or my husband, but I've got Hummer and Taser as well.
(gentle rock music)
^- [Kathleen] Tropical Depression Harvey began to form
^in the Gulf of Mexico on August 19th.
^All weather models predicted Harvey would make landfall
^on the Texas coast as a category four hurricane.
On August 25th, Harvey made landfall as a category four,
and would be considered the largest natural disaster
to hit the state of Texas in more than 100 years.
Rockport, Port Aransas, and Corpus Christi were hit hard
by winds reaching speeds of 100 plus miles per hour.
- [Commentator] It's kinda hard to talk right now.
Look at all this rain. See the debris.
(sound of wind drowns out speaker)
- [Kathleen] The hurricane also dropped
more than 51 inches of rain on southeast Texas.
The damage and devastation across the Texas coast
cost thousands their homes
and took the lives of more than 75 people.
Houston, Port Arthur, Beaumont, and other
southeast Texas areas were hit hardest with flood waters.
On August 21st, the Texas Military Department
activated 3,000 guardsmen in anticipation
of the damage and flooding that would be caused.
- (mumbles) When this first started, our primary mission
was search and rescue.
A tremendous amount of assets coming into
^the theater to do search and rescue.
^First thing we're gonna do is save lives.
(dramatic music)
- Well, we're just gonna do it.
^That's the right thing to do.
^We're here to, for a support.
^Regards to whether it is war time, peace time, or doing any
type of evacuation, which we're really here to do that.
- [Abbott] I authorized the deployment of all
of the Texas National Guard to address the challenges
that Texans are facing, all the way
from Corpus Christi to Houston, Texas.
- [Kathleen] More than 17,000 guardsmen were activated.
Their mission, to conduct ground and air missions,
evacuations, running supply distribution points,
and evacuation shelters across Texas.
More than 5,000 guardsmen from across the country
were also sent in to help the Texas Guard
with hurricane response operations.
(dramatic music)
Flood waters ranged from three to five feet deep.
Using aircraft, high water vehicles, and boats,
guardsmen helped rescue more than 16,000 people,
evacuate more than 18,000, and sheltered more than 26,000.
- We did hoist operations with aircraft.
At one point, we had 160 aircraft, broidery wing aircraft,
30 C-130 aircraft for evacuation.
We evacuated the city of Galveston.
- [Kathleen] 12 hundred animals were also rescued,
and more than 700 were sheltered.
The National Guard worked hand-in-hand
with civilian first responders to insure
residents effected by Hurricane Harvey were taken care of.
29 guard-supported distribution points
were set up throughout the Gulf coast.
Guardsmen distributed 214,000 cases of clean drinking water,
215,000 bags of ice, 129,000 cases of food,
and other essential supplies
to more than 100,000 Texas families.
- We divided them, evacuation capability, additional
resources because they don't have water or food.
We're out points keeping water, food, ice,
just to sustain them until the utilities
and the infrastructure can come back.
- [Kathleen] Even stranded livestock received aid.
Food was airlifted in to animals that couldn't be evacuated.
(dramatic music)
By the middle of September, Texas showed the world
how cooperation between guardsmen from different states,
first responders, and civilians face adversity.
- We have not denied a single request for support
on the ground or a single request for support from the air.
So, yes, I'd say it's been a very successful operation.
- [Kathleen] Texas now stands as a shining example
of how people can overcome their differences
and help out their fellow Texans.
- You guys saved our lives. I thank you so much.
(dramatic music)
